tax_name: General Sales Tax (GST) / الضريبة العامة على المبيعات — a VAT-type general sales tax with input-tax credit
legal_ref: General Sales Tax Law No. 6 of 1994 and amendments, Art. 6(a)
quote: "ما نسبة الضريبة العامة المفروضة؟ فرضت المادة (6/أ) من القانون ضريبة عامة على استيراد أي سلعة أو خدمة أو بيع أي منهما بنسبة (16%) من قيمة هذه السلعة أو بدل هذه الخدمة" — Art. 6(a) of the law imposes a general tax on the import or sale of any good or service at 16% of its value (ISTD FAQ on GST Law No. 6/1994; PDF uses a legacy Arabic font, text read from glyphs)
source_title: Income and Sales Tax Department (ISTD) – 'General questions on General Sales Tax Law No. 6 of 1994 and its amendments' (Wayback Machine copy, listing captured July 2026; istd.gov.jo refused connections)

reduced_rates.scope: specified goods set by Council of Ministers decision (per ISTD FAQ, 2016 snapshot)
goods/services in Schedule 2 of the law; exports; sales to Aqaba Special Economic Zone registrants

notes: Jordan levies a general sales tax rather than a tax called VAT, but it is a multi-stage consumption tax on supplies and imports of goods and services with deduction of input tax by registered persons, so recorded as has_vat true. A separate 'special tax' (الضريبة الخاصة) applies to Schedule-1 goods/services (tobacco, alcohol, mobile subscriptions, etc.), some of which also bear general tax. Various other reduced rates (e.g. 5%, 8%, 10%) exist for specific goods by Cabinet regulation; not individually verified. Aqaba Special Economic Zone has its own lower sales tax regime.
unverified: Date the 16% rate took effect not found in an official text (believed to be mid-2000s)

Full current list of reduced rates (Cabinet decisions) not verified; only 4% and 0% confirmed, from a 2016 ISTD FAQ page (https://web.archive.org/web/20161015082546/http://www.istd.gov.jo/Arabic/FrequentlyQuestions/FAQSales.aspx)
